newsitem.title: EGYPT: AmEx Bank Egypt raising 200 mln pounds in bonds.
newsitem.headline: AmEx Bank Egypt raising 200 mln pounds in bonds.

text.p: American Express Bank in Egypt said on Wednesday it planned to raise 200 million pounds ($59 million) by selling five-year floating-rate bonds.
The interest rate will be linked at three-month intervals to the average annualised yield on the most recent 91-day treasury bills. The yield on the latest bills was 10.256 percent.
If the treasury stops issuing bills, the interest will be 3.5 percentage points below the central bank discount rate, which has been stable at 13.5 percent since November 1995.
The offer will open on September 11 and stay open for at least the statutory 10 days and at the most two months.
The public sector Arab Land bank, behind the most recent bond offering on the Egyptian market, is offering floating-rate seven-year bonds at 1.5 percentage points below the discount rate.
The treasury is also about to issue medium-term bonds worth four billion pounds and Finance Minister Mohieddin el-Gharib has said the interest rate will be 11 percent.
